prompt_text:
Assume the role of a cyber threat intelligence annotation expert.
Given the provided text, extract named entities using ONLY the four categories specified below:
- Vulnerability: a CVE identifier for a known vulnerability. Use the canonical "CVE-YYYY-NNNN" format (e.g., CVE-2021-44228) and exact verbatim variants appearing in the text, including: pluralized "CVEs-YYYY-NNNN" (e.g., CVEs-2019-19781), alternate casing (e.g., cve-2021-44228), or IDs within parentheses/brackets (e.g., (CVE-2023-3519)). Named vulnerabilities (e.g., "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions are NOT Vulnerabilities. Only exact verbatim CVE-substring variants from input are valid entity text; normalized_id MUST map the variant to standard "CVE-YYYY-NNNN" (e.g., "CVEs-2019-19781" → "CVE-2019-19781").
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or core flaw class.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that may be impacted by vulnerabilities. Generic filenames, IPs, ports, or arbitrary strings not clearly identifiable as affected products/components are excluded (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe" excluded unless explicitly a product/component).
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, TA0011) or explicitly named attack method. Each distinct ID must be its own entity with only the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately). Sub-technique (T1090.002) and parent (T1090) IDs are valid when explicitly present. Only exact MITRE T-code/TA-code substrings qualify; do NOT tag software/tool IDs like S0508, S1063, S1054.

Constraints:
1. Entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring of the input.
2. Use 0-based start and exclusive end character offsets so text[start:end] equals entity text exactly.
3. normalized_id is the canonical identifier when available (standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI, or T-code); for CVE variants normalize to "CVE-YYYY-NNNN"; else null.
4. Do not emit duplicate entries for the same mention span.
5. Extract only entities meeting the strict definitions; skip non-conforming spans.
6. For AttackTechnique, capture only the exact ID token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078"), never surrounding words.
7. Never infer or insert entities absent as exact substrings; no hallucinated configs, products, vuln names, or technique IDs.
8. Each entity object MUST include the following required machine-readable fields: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id. The "id" field must be a unique string (e.g., "E1", "E2") assigned sequentially to each extracted entity. These six fields are mandatory and must always be present.
9. Optional provenance keys (such as "evidence" or "notes") MAY be included in entity objects if available from source annotation, but they are NOT required for your output. If you do not have such provenance, omit them. The evaluation gold set may contain extra keys like "evidence" or "notes"; those are annotations for human reference and do not change the required schema. Your output is valid as long as all mandatory fields (id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id) are present and correct. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema unless they are the optional provenance keys noted above.
10. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings.
